requirement: Validate the Tsay test against reference values from a recognized implementation such as R `TSA::Tsay.test`, and against simulations
note: Satisfied. R 4.3.3 with TSA 1.3.1 was installed in this container and `TSA::Tsay.test` was run on six series, four synthetic and two taken from the real frozen data (INDPRO and GDPC1 growth on their initial estimation windows). The Python statistic and p-value agree with R on all six to every significant digit R reports: TSA stores its results rounded to four significant figures, and the agreement is exact at that precision (worst relative error on the statistic 2.7e-4, consistent with the rounding alone). The 5% decision agrees on every case. The R reference values are stored in tests/fixtures/tsay_reference_cases.json with the R and TSA versions that produced them, so the test runs without R present.

requirement: Full baseline execution runtime on the approved sample
note: Not a requirement failure: Comp §9 requires per-stage runtime reporting, which row C9 verifies as complete. This row records a fact for scheduling the Part 8 run. Measured cost of one MSAR fit on this 4-core container: K=2, p=4, n=240 takes 6.2s; K=3, p=4, n=240 takes 25.5s and n=955 takes 110.5s. With roughly 700 monthly origins per series the K=3 robustness chains dominate, so a complete baseline run is a multi-hour job even with the fit cache, warm starts and four workers. This is a Part 8 scheduling matter, not a methodological problem, and no approved parameter was changed to reduce it.
